name: HubSpot
one_liner: CRM and marketing platform with contacts, deals, and a large public developer API.

one_liner.note: HubSpot marketing site for the CRM platform.

auth.note: OAuth is required for multiple accounts, while static auth access tokens are used for installing in a single account at a time.
You can use service keys to query HubSpot's REST APIs directly.

access.note: Create and manage service keys in the HubSpot account; no vendor review is required to start calling the API.

api_surface.note: Example REST request to api.hubapi.com with a Bearer access token.
HubSpot documents a GraphQL API for querying CRM and CMS data.

mcp.note: The HubSpot MCP server is at https://mcp.hubspot.com and uses OAuth with PKCE.

verdict.note: Public docs and self-serve credentials (OAuth apps or service keys) exist, so a toolkit can be built today.

notes: Customer super-admins install apps or create keys. Marketplace listing is optional and is not the path to credentials. Service keys are REST-only; GraphQL is documented for apps/private tokens. MCP OAuth is in addition to API auth, which already includes OAuth2.
label_notes: Straightforward official docs. GraphQL is included because HubSpot documents it as a public query API, not only CMS page data.

name: DealCloud
one_liner: Intapp deal-management CRM used by capital-markets and deal teams, with a documented REST API.

auth.note: DealCloud uses the OAuth2 Client Credentials flow to generate a bearer token.
Click Enable in the API Key section of the user Profile, then copy the API key.

access.note: If you do not see the Admin section, contact your organization's admin or DealCloud Customer Success Manager (CSM). Credentials require an existing DealCloud tenant.

api_surface.note: REST token endpoint at /api/rest/v1/oauth/token and data/schema APIs under /api/rest/v4/.

mcp.note: Default MCP endpoint: https://[tenant].my.intapp.com/mcp/celeste/DealCloud. Requires a Celeste license.

verdict.note: The API is documented, but usable access depends on a DealCloud site and CSM/admin enablement.

notes: API keys are enabled per user after an admin turns on the API capability. Official MCP requires a Celeste license and MCP Access. Getting a DealCloud tenant is a sales/CSM path, not self-serve signup.
label_notes: Public docs exist, so this is gated_sales + buildable_with_approval, not no_public_api. Official MCP is easy to miss if only the REST pages are read.

name: Zendesk
one_liner: Customer support platform with ticketing, help center, and a long-standing public REST API.

auth.note: OAuth is the recommended authentication method; Zendesk supports authorization code and client credentials.
Zendesk API tokens will be permanently deactivated on April 30, 2027; migrate to OAuth.
API tokens are still a documented way to authenticate Ticketing, Help Center, and Voice APIs.

access.note: API tokens are created in Admin Center; OAuth clients can also be registered there. A developer can start from a Zendesk account without a partner program.

api_surface.note: Official Zendesk API reference covering Ticketing and related REST APIs.

mcp.note: Connect to the Zendesk MCP server using a URL such as https://example.zendesk.com/mcp. Zendesk Bridge / external AI agents are in an early access program.

verdict.note: Documented REST API and self-serve credentials exist.

notes: API tokens remain valid until 30 Apr 2027 and are listed as api_key. The official MCP server is in an EAP (join External AI EAP); it is a real documented server URL, not a vague mention. A separate Zendesk MCP client article describes Zendesk connecting to external MCP servers, which is not a Zendesk-hosted server.
label_notes: MCP is official despite EAP because docs give a real server URL and setup steps. API tokens are still documented, so auth_methods includes api_key as well as oauth2.

name: Pylon
one_liner: B2B support platform that unifies Slack, email, and other channels into one queue, with a public REST API.

one_liner.note: Pylon product site describing B2B support across Slack, Teams, email, and WhatsApp.

auth.note: The Pylon API uses Bearer authentication. Generate an API token in the Pylon dashboard.

access.note: Professional and Advanced plans say Book a demo; Enterprise is Talk to sales. FAQ: free trials are set up by a sales representative. Standard contracts are annual.
Only Admins can create and manage API tokens, and only after a Pylon workspace exists.

api_surface.note: Official Pylon API docs; US base URL https://api.usepylon.com.

mcp.note: Official Pylon MCP Server at https://mcp.usepylon.com (US) and https://mcp.eu.usepylon.com (EU). Auth: OAuth 2.0 or an API token.

verdict.note: API and MCP are included on paid plans, but there is no self-serve checkout; access goes through sales or a sales-set trial.

notes: OAuth 2.0 is documented for the MCP server, not as a way to call the developer API, so it is not listed in auth_methods. Pricing lists API and MCP on Professional and Advanced, but checkout is Book a demo / Talk to sales.
label_notes: Clear sales gate despite excellent public API and official MCP docs. Do not treat published seat prices as self_serve_paid, because you cannot buy without sales.

name: Slack
one_liner: Team messaging platform with channels, DMs, and a large public Web API and app ecosystem.

auth.note: Slack documents OAuth for apps and token types including bot tokens, which are treated as api_key.

access.note: Developers can create Slack apps and obtain tokens from the app settings without a vendor partner review.

api_surface.note: Slack Web API methods are documented HTTP RPC-style REST endpoints.

mcp.note: Official Slack MCP server. Workspace admins approve MCP client integrations.

verdict.note: Documented API and self-serve app creation exist.

notes: Workspace admin approval is an install step (requires_end_user_admin), not a vendor credential gate. Bot tokens and other app tokens are listed under api_key. Official MCP lives at docs.slack.dev.
label_notes: Standard self-serve OAuth app case. The official MCP docs are on docs.slack.dev, not only api.slack.com.

name: WhatsApp Business
one_liner: Meta's WhatsApp Business Platform Cloud API for sending and receiving business messages.

auth.note: Generate an access token and optionally a system user permanent token; send Authorization: Bearer on graph.facebook.com.
Embedded Signup exchanges an authorization code for a token via /oauth/access_token, which is the OAuth path for onboarding other businesses.

access.note: If you are building an app that other businesses will be using, you must request Advanced access and submit the app to App Review. Direct developers using the API for themselves do not need Advanced access.

api_surface.note: Cloud API HTTP calls to graph.facebook.com/.../messages with a JSON body.

mcp.note: Official WhatsApp Cloud API docs were checked; no official MCP server, installable repo, or dedicated MCP docs page was found.

verdict.note: A documented API exists, but a multi-tenant toolkit that onboards other businesses needs App Review / Advanced access.

notes: System user and dashboard access tokens are listed as api_key. OAuth is listed because Embedded Signup's documented token exchange is how third-party apps obtain credentials for customer WhatsApp accounts. A developer can start in test mode for their own portfolio without App Review, but permission to call the API as a third-party / multi-tenant app requires Meta's review. No official MCP server was found.
label_notes: Labelled gated_partner (not self_serve) because the rubric treats third-party / multi-tenant permission that needs vendor app review as a partner gate. Direct-developer self-serve test access is real but is not the toolkit path.

name: Mailchimp
one_liner: Email marketing and audience platform with a public Marketing REST API.

auth.note: Every request to the Marketing API carries a credential. There are two kinds: an API key, and OAuth 2.
OAuth 2 lets your application access Marketing API data on behalf of another Mailchimp user; it is how third-party integrations work.

access.note: Generate an API key in your Mailchimp account under API Keys, or register an OAuth app. No vendor review is required to start.

api_surface.note: Marketing API requests go to https://api.mailchimp.com/3.0/.

mcp.note: This documentation site is itself an MCP server at https://mailchimp.com/developer/_mcp/server. It searches published docs, not a Mailchimp account.

verdict.note: Documented REST API and self-serve API keys / OAuth apps exist.

notes: HTTP Basic is only a transport for the same API key or OAuth token (anystring:TOKEN), not a separate auth method. The official MCP server answers questions from the docs site and does not act on an account; account automation still goes through the Marketing API. OAuth is required for third-party / marketplace integrations.
label_notes: Docs-only official MCP still counts as official under the rubric (real vendor-published server URL). Notes explain the limited scope so it is not confused with an account-control MCP.

name: LinkedIn Ads
one_liner: LinkedIn Marketing / Advertising APIs for ad accounts, campaigns, and conversions.

one_liner.note: Official LinkedIn Marketing API documentation on Microsoft Learn.

auth.note: All listed Marketing API permissions are Member Permissions (3-legged OAuth). See Authorization Code Flow.

access.note: Advertising API and several other products are open to all approved developers — apply through the standard process. All applications start with Development tier.
LinkedIn reviews the access-request form, business, and use case before advertising API access is granted.

api_surface.note: Versioned LinkedIn Marketing REST APIs on Microsoft Learn.

mcp.note: Official LinkedIn Marketing API docs were checked; no vendor-published MCP server or MCP docs page was found.

verdict.note: A documented OAuth API exists, but developers must apply and be approved before they get usable Advertising API access.

notes: Development-tier access still requires LinkedIn's developer-application approval, so this is gated_partner rather than self_serve. Standard-tier upgrades go through Developer Support. No official MCP documentation was found; unofficial third-party posts are not used as evidence of an official server.
label_notes: Classic partner/developer-approval gate. Do not label self_serve just because docs and an apply form are public.

name: Shopify
one_liner: Commerce platform for online stores, with Admin GraphQL and legacy REST APIs for apps.

auth.note: Apps get an access token after a merchant installs the app and approves scopes. Tokens are obtained at the OAuth token endpoint.
Admin-created custom apps receive an access token generated in the Shopify admin (legacy custom apps can no longer be created, but existing ones are maintained).

access.note: Partners can create apps and obtain tokens through install/OAuth without a mandatory App Store review. App Store listing is a separate, optional distribution path.

api_surface.note: GraphQL Admin API at /admin/api/{version}/graphql.json, authenticated with X-Shopify-Access-Token.
REST Admin API is a legacy API as of October 1, 2024, but it is still documented. New public apps must use GraphQL.

mcp.note: Storefront Catalog MCP is an official MCP server at https://{storedomain}/api/ucp/mcp for searching a merchant catalog.
A separate 'Shopify MCP' admin-style product is documented as coming soon and is not publicly available yet.

verdict.note: Documented Admin APIs and self-serve partner/app credentials exist.

notes: Merchant install approval is requires_end_user_admin, not a vendor gate. REST is still documented, so api_types includes rest and graphql; new public apps are GraphQL-only. The coming-soon Admin Shopify MCP is a vague mention and would be none on its own; mcp_status is official because Storefront Catalog MCP is a real documented vendor server. Legacy admin-created custom app tokens are listed as api_key.
label_notes: Do not label MCP as none just because the Admin 'Shopify MCP' page says coming soon. Storefront Catalog MCP is already official. Access stays self_serve because credentials do not require App Store review.

name: fanbasis
one_liner: Creator payments and checkout platform now branded Commas (formerly FanBasis), with a public REST API.

one_liner.note: On July 14, 2026, FanBasis became Commas. Commas is operated by FanBasis, Inc.

auth.note: Get your API key: log into your Commas dashboard and go to Account → API Keys. Requests use the x-api-key header.

access.note: New users can create an account on commas.com. API keys are created in the dashboard; no partner review is described.

api_surface.note: REST examples such as POST https://www.fanbasis.com/public-api/checkout-sessions with x-api-key.

mcp.note: Current official Commas API docs were checked; no official MCP server or dedicated MCP docs page was found. Third-party 'Comma' report-tool MCP pages are a different product.

verdict.note: Public API reference and self-serve API keys exist.

notes: FanBasis rebranded to Commas on 14 Jul 2026; production API host still includes www.fanbasis.com/public-api. Older FanBasis docs at dev-docs.fanbasis.com show a login page, but the current official API reference at commasdocs.com is public. No official MCP server was found.
label_notes: The earlier expectation was password-gated docs and possibly no public API. As of this labelling pass, official docs are public and the API is self-serve with an API key. Labelled from current official docs, not the outdated login wall. Identity stays slug fanbasis / name fanbasis per the frozen CSV.

name: Firecrawl
one_liner: Web-scraping and crawling API that turns sites into LLM-ready data, with official MCP support.

auth.note: API keys (Authorization: Bearer fc-...) and OAuth for apps, whose fco_ access tokens work on the REST API in place of an API key. MCP-only OAuth is a separate flow that does not work on the REST API.

access.note: Free plan is self-serve signup with monthly credits; no vendor review required to create an API key.

api_surface.note: REST API at https://api.firecrawl.dev/v2/...

mcp.note: Hosted official MCP at https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp.

verdict.note: Documented REST API and self-serve credentials exist.

notes: primary_auth is oauth2 because OAuth for apps is a documented way for third-party apps to call the product's REST API (fco_ access tokens). API keys remain a documented method. A separate MCP sign-in flow issues credentials that are not valid on the REST API, so that flow is not treated as API auth. Some scrape/search endpoints also allow keyless calls with tight limits.
label_notes: OAuth-as-primary follows the rubric preference, even though API keys are the common first example in the docs.

name: Clay
one_liner: Data-enrichment workspace with a public REST API, CLI, and official MCP server.

auth.note: Every request to the Clay Public API must include a Clay API key in the clay-api-key header.

access.note: Create an API key in Clay under API and CLI → API keys, or with the clay CLI.
Self-serve plans include a free option and paid plans with Start 14-day trial or buy now.

api_surface.note: Public API example: GET https://api.clay.com/public/v0/me with clay-api-key.

mcp.note: Clay exposes an MCP server at https://api.clay.com/v3/mcp. Dynamic Client Registration is the self-service OAuth path onto that server.

verdict.note: Public API docs and self-serve API keys exist.

notes: MCP uses OAuth 2.1 with Dynamic Client Registration; that OAuth flow authenticates the MCP server, not the Public API, so oauth2 is not listed in auth_methods. Workspace admins can restrict allowed MCP clients; that is an install policy, not a vendor credential gate.
label_notes: The sample was picked as a hard case because a public self-serve API was not obvious at selection time. Official Public API docs at developers.clay.com now exist and are self-serve, including on the free plan, so the honest current label is buildable_now.

name: GitHub
one_liner: Hosted Git hosting and collaboration platform with REST and GraphQL APIs and an official MCP server.

auth.note: The REST API can be authenticated with a personal access token, OAuth token, or GitHub App installation token.
GitHub Apps authenticate as the app by signing a short-lived JWT with the app's private key.

access.note: Developers can create PATs, OAuth apps, and GitHub Apps from a GitHub account without a vendor sales process.

api_surface.note: Official GitHub REST API documentation.
Official GitHub GraphQL API documentation.

mcp.note: Official GitHub MCP server repository in the github org.
GitHub docs for setting up the official GitHub MCP Server.

verdict.note: Documented APIs and self-serve credentials exist.

notes: Personal access tokens are api_key. GitHub App JWTs are jwt_service_account. Organization owners may need to approve GitHub App installs (requires_end_user_admin), which is not a vendor gate.
label_notes: All three auth methods are documented official API auth, so they are all listed. primary_auth is oauth2 per the preference rule.

name: Snowflake
one_liner: Cloud data platform with documented SQL, REST APIs, multiple auth methods, and a managed MCP server.

auth.note: REST requests can authenticate with key-pair JWTs, OAuth tokens, or programmatic access tokens (PATs).

access.note: Snowflake offers trial accounts a developer can create in order to start using the platform, including API access, without a sales contract.

api_surface.note: Snowflake REST APIs, e.g. https://{account}.snowflakecomputing.com/api/v2/databases, with a Bearer token.

mcp.note: The Snowflake-managed MCP server lets AI agents retrieve data from Snowflake accounts. OAuth is the default, with optional PATs.

verdict.note: Documented REST APIs and a self-serve trial path exist.

notes: PATs are listed as api_key. Key-pair authentication (signed JWT) is jwt_service_account. Workload identity federation is also documented and is noted here rather than added as custom_other. Account admins configure users, roles, and network policies (requires_end_user_admin). A free trial that already includes API access is self_serve, even though paid editions exist.
label_notes: Access is self_serve because a trial account can be created and used for API/MCP work without talking to sales. Enterprise contracts exist later but are not required to get credentials.

name: Notion
one_liner: Collaborative workspace for docs and databases, with a public REST API and official MCP server.

auth.note: Public integrations use OAuth 2.0 so users can grant a third-party app access to their workspace.
Internal connections use a static integration token generated in the developer portal.

access.note: Developers can create public or internal integrations from a Notion account without a vendor review to obtain credentials.

api_surface.note: Official Notion REST API and integration docs.

mcp.note: Official hosted Notion MCP server (mcp.notion.com) with an OAuth PKCE flow.

verdict.note: Documented API and self-serve integration credentials exist.

notes: Internal integration tokens are api_key. Users must grant a connection access to pages; workspace admins can restrict integrations (requires_end_user_admin). MCP OAuth is in addition to API OAuth, which is already documented for public integrations.
label_notes: Standard self-serve public API plus official MCP.

name: Smartsheet
one_liner: Work-management and spreadsheet-style collaboration platform with a REST API on paid plans.

auth.note: Generate an API access token in Personal Settings > API Access and send it as Authorization: Bearer.
OAuth authorization-code flow at https://app.smartsheet.com/b/authorize, with token exchange at POST /token.

access.note: Required plan: Business, Enterprise, or Advanced Work Management.
Business plan is listed with a Start now checkout and includes API calls. Enterprise is Contact us. Pro does not include API calls.

api_surface.note: Official Smartsheet REST API at https://api.smartsheet.com/2.0.

mcp.note: Official MCP server at https://mcp.smartsheet.com (US), also requiring a Business or higher plan.

verdict.note: A developer can buy the Business plan online and then create API tokens or an OAuth app, with no human vendor review.

notes: API access is plan-gated to Business and above, but Business can be purchased online, so access is self_serve_paid rather than gated_sales. Paid-plan API access is not an engineering blocker, so the verdict is buildable_now. Personal tokens are api_key.
label_notes: This was selected to test self_serve_paid vs gated_sales. Pricing 'Start now' on Business plus 'API calls' in the plan table supports self_serve_paid.

name: Stripe
one_liner: Payments platform with a comprehensive public API, Connect OAuth, and an official MCP server.

auth.note: The Stripe API uses API keys to authenticate requests. Keys can be sent with HTTP Basic or as a Bearer token.
Connect OAuth is the documented way for third-party platforms to obtain access to connected Stripe accounts and call the Stripe API on their behalf.

access.note: API keys are created in the Stripe Dashboard after a self-serve signup; test keys are available immediately.

api_surface.note: Official Stripe HTTP API reference.

mcp.note: Official Stripe MCP server at https://mcp.stripe.com, with OAuth or an agent API key.

verdict.note: Documented API and self-serve Dashboard keys exist.

notes: Secret and restricted keys are api_key; HTTP Basic is only a transport for those keys, not a separate method. primary_auth is oauth2 because Connect OAuth is documented for third-party / multi-tenant apps calling the Stripe API. First-party integrations often start with a secret key. Workload Identity Federation is also documented and is mentioned here rather than as custom_other. MCP can use OAuth or an agent API key.
label_notes: OAuth-as-primary is a rubric call, not because keys are undocumented. An implementation that started with api_key would still need oauth2 in auth_methods to be complete.

name: PitchBook
one_liner: Private-capital market data platform with a contract-gated research API and an official Data MCP offering.

auth.note: The team helps you establish the API connection through an API key or authentication token.

access.note: Our API is a separate offering from the PitchBook Platform that requires a standalone contract agreement. To start, send a request to the Direct Data team.

api_surface.note: The PitchBook API is a RESTful implementation. Every call uses the same base URL: https://api.pitchbook.com.

mcp.note: PitchBook Data MCP is currently live and available to customers upon request.

verdict.note: A documented REST API exists, but credentials require a sales contract / Direct Data request.

notes: Help pages describe an API key or authentication token; these are listed as api_key. Official MCP is announced as available to customers on request. Help-center and press pages are official sources for a product whose detailed API reference is otherwise contract-gated. 'Gated, with evidence' is sufficient; we did not obtain a key.
label_notes: Classic gated_sales research API. MCP labelled official from the vendor press announcement (allowed as official announcement). Third-party MCP gateway writeups were not used as the primary source.

name: Reducto
one_liner: Document-parsing and extraction API for PDFs and similar files, with official MCP servers.

auth.note: Create an API key in Reducto Studio under API Keys. Send Authorization: Bearer $REDUCTO_API_KEY.

access.note: Sign up for a free account at https://studio.reducto.ai and create an API key in the docs or Studio.
Standard plan is self-serve pay-as-you-go with included free usage credits.

api_surface.note: REST example: POST https://platform.reducto.ai/parse with a Bearer API key.

mcp.note: Official hosted MCP server at https://mcp.reducto.ai/mcp, plus a local uvx MCP server.

verdict.note: Documented API and self-serve signup / API keys exist.

notes: The local MCP login flow can open a browser, but API calls themselves use an API key, including on the hosted MCP (Authorization: Bearer). SDKs wrap the same HTTP API, so api_types is rest, not sdk_only.
label_notes: Clean self-serve developer API. Composio catalog snapshot has no toolkit (status none).

name: NotebookLM
one_liner: Google's notebook product for researching and chatting with sources, now also called Gemini Notebook, with a preview public API.

one_liner.note: Gemini Notebook API is a REST interface for creating and managing notebooks and sources in Gemini Notebook (NotebookLM).

auth.note: The Gemini Notebook API uses OAuth 2.0. Every request must include an OAuth 2.0 Bearer token. The API doesn't accept API keys.

access.note: During the preview, the API is available for personal Google Accounts. Google Workspace accounts are not yet supported. You can enable the API in a Google Cloud project you create yourself.

api_surface.note: REST at https://notebook.googleapis.com/v1 for notebooks and sources.

mcp.note: Official MCP server documentation for the Gemini Notebook API (hosted at notebook.googleapis.com/mcp).

verdict.note: Early Access Public Preview: the Gemini Notebook API and MCP server are in an early access Public Preview.

notes: Do not confuse the consumer NotebookLM app with unrelated Gemini generative-language APIs. Two official notebook APIs exist: (1) the Gemini Notebook API on developers.google.com/notebook, personal-account Public Preview, which this row follows; (2) Gemini Notebook Enterprise / NotebookLM Enterprise on Google Cloud (v1alpha, also marked Preview / Pre-GA, and license-gated). The Enterprise path is recorded as an acceptable alternative. Preview is the main blocker on the self-serve path.
label_notes: Hard judgement: the public personal API and the Enterprise API are both previews. Primary label uses the personal Gemini Notebook API (self_serve + not_buildable + preview_or_unstable + official MCP). The acceptable alternative is the Enterprise reading: gated_sales + buildable_with_approval + gated_access, which matches the assignment hint of an Enterprise API and the blocker-priority rule when a license gate and a preview both apply.

acceptable_alternatives.notes: Enterprise / NotebookLM Enterprise API on Google Cloud is documented REST (v1alpha) but is Preview/Pre-GA and requires Gemini Notebook Enterprise licenses. That license path is a sales/admin gate. When both a license gate and a preview apply, gated_access is the main blocker. Official MCP in this alternative is none unless Enterprise-specific MCP docs are cited; the personal Gemini Notebook MCP is a different offering.
